case_name: Ms. Jordan Diengdeh vs S.S. Chopra
facts_of_case: Petitioner, a Christian woman, married to respondent, a Sikh man, under Indian Christian Marriage Act 1872. She filed petition for declaration of nullity of marriage or judicial separation on ground of impotence of her husband. Trial court rejected prayer for nullity but granted decree for judicial separation on ground of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage appears to have broken down irretrievably when the parties are unable to live together.
legal_principles.held: At this stage, we are not concerned with the question how far the wife has been able to establish her case. The real problem now is that the marriage appears to have broken down irretrievably.

legal_principles.principle: A decree for dissolution of marriage can be granted only on the grounds specified in the Indian Divorce Act.
legal_principles.held: The ground on which a husband may obtain a decree for dissolution of marriage is the adultery of the wife. The grounds on which a wife may obtain a decree for dissolution of marriage are change of religion from Christianity to another religion and marriage with another woman, incestuous adultery, bigamy with adultery, marriage with another woman with adultery, rape, sodomy or bestiality, adultery coupled with cruelty, adultery coupled with desertion for more than two years.

legal_principles.principle: A declaration of nullity of marriage can be granted on the ground of impotence of the husband.
legal_principles.held: Section 19 provides that a marriage may be declared null and void on the ground-(1) that the respondent was impotent at the time of the institution of the suit;

legal_principles.principle: A decree for judicial separation can be granted on the ground of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: A decree for judicial separation was granted on the ground of cruelty.

outcome.final_order: Supreme Court held irretrievable break-down of marriage.
